title: Old Wood
subtitle: Quick, get out there before the cakes sell out.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Knock, knock! Which would make the world a better place, art or a heart of gold? Ha-ha! Neither! The little knocker-upper, Flutterpage, will!
Flutterpage knocks on Willow's back door, but she receives no answer.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm? Where's Ms. Willow? She should be warmin' up by now.
She walks a short loop around the perimeter of the house.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Where's she gone? Ms. Willow! Ms. Wiiillooow!
Silence.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Knock, knock! Don't jump to conclusions. Mr. Wind will tell you the truth.
A gust of wind picks Flutterpage up, raising her high in the air. She sways as she glides in through an open window.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Knock, knock! I'll open all the windows and doors, and all the treasure chests, too. Ms. Willow! Ms. Willow?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow! What you doin' over there?
In a dark corner, Willow stands silently before a peculiar object. She senses Flutterpage but doesn't turn her head.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You're early. Why am I not surprised? You're about as patient as a dog waiting for his dinner.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I thought you'd start practicin' as soon as you woke up. What you doin' in this corner?
Willow softly rests her hand upon the item before her.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Come take a look at this. I wonder if it still works.
The peculiar item sits still.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm. What a strange thing! What is it?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: It's a sort of instrument called the didgeriwood. Come give it a try. First, put your hand on it like this.
Flutterpage, imitating Willow, lays her hand on the didgeriwood.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Okay. Then what?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I'll teach you how to play it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It's beautiful, like raindrops patterin' on tree leaves.
Willow gently puts Flutterpage's hand aside before resting her own hand on it again.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm? Why's it gone quiet all of a sudden?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: It's broken.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What?! I didn't break it, did I?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: No. It's been broken for a long time.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Well, judgin' by the look of it, it must be old. It's got mildew all over.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: This instrument is crucial to every Floor Ritualist. You see, we're not just dancers but music makers, using our arcane skills to play the didgeriwood while we dance.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: *sigh*

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Don't worry, Ms. Willow. I know broken things ain't always easy to fix, but we can start with the easy part. Why don't we wipe off the dust first?
Flutterpage picks up a loose piece of paper and moves to wipe the dust from the didgeriwood.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Huh? Is this ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: The athlete registration form for the qualifiers?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Um ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh!
The girl blinks, her hair jutting out in every direction. She pauses for a moment as she slowly reads the paper.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: And look! You ain't submitted it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Why not?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: There's still time, isn't there?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: No! You already missed the window!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Blimey, we've got to do somethin' about this! Hmm. Oh! That's right! Mr. Fog said that two officers from the Australian headquarters would arrive in London today. I think we can ask them to pull the ... What was the word?
Willow doesn't respond.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Anyway, we need to get a move on! I'll pull you up.
Flutterpage tugs desperately at Willow, who steadfastly holds her ground, leaving them at an impasse.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Flutterpage ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Maybe it's time to give up.
Flutterpage turns her head.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Give up?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What do you mean, "give up"?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I don't understand.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ain't this the Uluru Games we've been talkin' about for ages?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Think of all the effort you've made. You didn't jump up and down in the garden over and over again to dust it, did you? You're an athlete, not a feather duster!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: A-And you finished that move! The, you know, the um ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The two-and-a-half turn with free leg backwards and upwards, wand throw and catch.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Yeah! That one!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: See? How can you just "give up"?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, please, don't look at me like that.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Yes, I've always dreamt of completing this element.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: No one knows better than I how much this means to me.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Then, why are you ...?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I don't want to talk about it.
Willow lowers her head.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You should leave. I need to see what I can do to fix the didgeriwood. Don't forget to close the door behind you.
Flutterpage stands frozen, staring at Willow for what feels like forever, before pouting angrily and crouching down, her arms firmly crossed.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I ain't leavin'.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I'm angry.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: *sigh*
Unsure of what to say, Willow lets the moment hang awkwardly in the air.
Beneath the painting of the Irish countryside, one stands and the other squats, the grandfather clock marking each passing second with its steady tick.
Eventually, Willow lightly taps Flutterpage on the head with her finger.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Don't be upset. It's not that serious.
Flutterpage continues to stare at the floor, shaking her head forcefully.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I ... I talked to Ms. Bartley yesterday.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You didn't ...
Flutterpage stands up.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Yeah, I challenged her on your behalf with a letter.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: She only visited me so she could show off all the titles she's won. She's not the first to come just to laugh in my face.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: That ain't true.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Caroline was happy when she got the letter.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She was really lookin' forward to competin' against you. She told me why, too.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She said you were the most talented and hard workin' player she'd ever seen, and that it took all her effort just to keep you in her sight, let alone catch up with you.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Because you're different, the one true master of the art. If there were only one gold medal in the history of the Floor Ritual, it'd be meant for you.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Those were her exact words.
She wrestles with her memories, yet the emotional pull of the past remains palpable.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I only chose to become a Floor Ritualist ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Because I had a talent for it. I wanted to win.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So I practiced and practiced, paying little attention to anything else.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: My family, my friends, my life, none of it mattered more than victory.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: To me, there was no reward more alluring than the euphoria of winning.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: But whenever I looked back at my past glories, I felt no happiness or excitement. Instead, I'd replay every moment in my mind, every lost point, every imperfect movement, and think about how close I was to failure.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: So I pursued the next victory even more fervently. I thought, "Next time, I won't lose a single point. Next time, I'll be perfect."

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: That was what was running through my mind when I was crowned champion of the Beltane.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: But there was no next time.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: That was my last competition.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But you can still have a next time. You can still try again. Look at you! Your skills haven't dulled a bit!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What's the point? I've pushed away everyone I wanted to honor with my victories. I've strayed too far from home.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Not to mention ... *sigh*
She casts a silent glance at her leg.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Okay, but are you happy when you do the Floor Ritual?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Am I happy?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: See, I love bein' a knocker-upper. Every mornin', I get to see all kinds of sleepin' positions: some people cuddle, others curl up in a ball, and some ain't even in bed at all.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I like watchin' them wake up, too. Like newborn kittens learnin' to crawl, hehe!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: And finally, when they completely open their eyes and stand on their feet, I feel a gust of fresh wind rushin' out the window.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It makes me happy.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So, what about you? Does the Floor Ritual make you happy?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I don't know.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The only thing that comes to mind is that, after a game, my mam would take me to the old cake shop down the road and buy me a cheesecake. The same one every time.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: That was the only time I'd allow myself to eat dessert.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Mhm.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: It had raspberries and chocolate drizzled on top. I can still remember the taste, sweet and tart, with a light bitterness.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ooooh.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So what really makes you happy is the cheesecake after the game!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Right, then let's get you registered for the qualifiers so you can have that post-game celebration cheesecake again!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What are you ...?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Let's go talk to Mr. Fog. I'm sure he can find a way to get you into the qualifiers. And if your leg's causin' you trouble or anythin', Ms. Tooth Fairy can help you out. She is a doctor from the Foundation, after all.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: W-Wait!
A delicate wind brushes past, causing her legs to lose their earlier stubbornness and follow Flutterpage out of the house.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm? Don't you want to eat that cheesecake?
They walk beside the paintings of Ireland.
They wind their way through the willow-bound torches and mysterious vessels.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Don't you think it'll make you happy?
They pass through the house's front door.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: That cheesecake ...
And leap out of the house.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It will, right? Then let's go get it! Life's all about happiness, ain't it?
A surge of fresh air floods Willow's nostrils, hitting her like a full-on collision with the outside world.
Lowering her gaze, she catches sight of Flutterpage hovering in the air, a delicate lock of hair swaying in the breeze.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You silly little Buzzie.
Using a hand spared from Flutterpage's tugging, Willow softly flicks at the silky strand of hair.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hmm? Why's everyone leavin' the stadium?
Flutterpage is still tugging Willow in the direction of the venue, but there seem to be more and more despondent people going in the other direction.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oi! Where you all goin'?

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Home.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Home? Why? Mr. Fog's holdin' the ribbon-cuttin' ceremony for his machine in the stadium. Why ain't you goin' there?

items.speaker: Will
items.text: It ain't happenin'.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Pardon?

items.speaker: Will
items.text: I said it ain't happenin'! The ceremony!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: The Foundation officers canceled the qualifiers.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Mr. Fog's so-called "biggest air purifier ever" doesn't work.
